title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of Chapter IX ('GF IX'; the 'GF' is probably the label of the series of notes) of Grothendieck's July 1986 notes on 'ateliers' ('workshops'). The ateliers are his axiomatic frame for a 'topologie modérée' (tame topology), the programme announced in §5 of Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The note 'voir p.75 la mise au pt sur la terminologie' shows the vocabulary was still moving.

The diagram is a taxonomy, a poset of classes of structures, ordered by specialisation from top to bottom.

Top: the general atelier, a quadruple (𝒜, ⊴, ≪, |∘|). From the next page and the neighbouring notes:
- 𝒜 is a class of 'objects' (regions or pieces).
- ⊴ is a parthood or inclusion preorder.
- ≪ is a 'well inside' or strict-inclusion relation (something like relative compactness or non-tangential part).
- |∘| is a 'meets/overlaps' relation; its negation is written with an overbar.

Forgetting part of the structure gives three branches:
- Spatial atelier (𝒜, ⊴, |∘|). Its associated ordered set Σ of 'sous-objets' (presumably the down-closed or Sup-generated sets of objects) is the space-like lattice.
- Local atelier (𝒜, ⊴, ≪, |∘|_ℒ). The meet relation is controlled by points ℒ.
- Faithful (fidèle) atelier (𝒜, ⊴, ≪).

A 'divisible' atelier appears just below the general one; it is perhaps crossed out.

Specialisations:
- Ponctuel atelier: Σ ≅ 𝔓(ℒ). The subobject lattice is a full power set of a set ℒ of points, i.e. an atomic complete Boolean algebra, a 'spatial' or sober situation.
- Ensembliste atelier (ℒ): objects are subsets of a set.
- Maquette: Σ ≅ 𝔓(𝒜), i.e. every family of objects is a subobject.
- Then modéré (tame) variants, 'at. ens. modéré', 'at. discret' and finally 'at.-point' (replacing a crossed-out 'at. trivial').
- The 'at. mod' / 'atelier modéré' node is placed with question marks. The boxed NB says that if tame ateliers are faithful, 'mod' sits between 'fidèle' and 'maquette'.

The text below the diagram sets the programme:
1. Focus on spatial ateliers, including set-theoretic ones such as those generated by 'ordered intervals' (the model of the o-minimal / semialgebraic line), and maquettes, judged 'primordial in certain respects'.
2. For tame work 'in the spirit of set-theoretic topology', restrict further to local ateliers. This excludes maquettes except discrete ones.
3. Towards a genuine tame topology, study tame ateliers, set-theoretic or not, which include maquettes.

The page continues overleaf: there one should probably assume that Σ is 'modular', in fact distributive in the infinite sense (A∧Sup B_i = Sup (A∧B_i), i.e. a frame or Boolean-type law), which might force faithfulness.

The question on the next page explains what this setup is for. Do points x ∈ ℒ give atoms of Σ*? Equivalently, are points separated by objects meeting one but not the other? This is a T1/sobriety-type separation question for point-free spaces.

In modern terms this is a point-free (mereotopological) axiomatics of 'regions' with parthood, contact/overlap and well-inside, designed to give a non-pathological topology. The page classifies the possible degrees of 'pointedness' and 'set-likeness'.
errors: No mathematical error: this is a planning taxonomy with explicit uncertainties ('?').
The placement of the tame (modéré) node is unresolved; Grothendieck himself gives two incompatible positions, conditional on whether tame implies faithful.
Some diagram arrows are dashed or doubtful, so the implications between classes are conjectural, not proved.
The claim that locality excludes maquettes except discrete ones is asserted without argument on this page.
Next page: calling the infinite distributive law 'modulaire' is a misnomer. A∧Sup B_i = Sup(A∧B_i) is the frame (infinite distributive) law, not modularity.

ideas.what: An axiomatic 'atelier' (𝒜, ⊴, ≪, |∘|): regions with parthood, well-inside and overlap relations as a foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology / contact algebras / region-based (point-free) topology; proximity and de Vries (compingent) algebras for ≪
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna (1922), de Vries (1962), Clarke (1981); later Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only the motivation (tame topology) is in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984); the atelier axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Hierarchy of special classes: spatial, local, faithful, ponctuel (Σ≅𝔓(ℒ)), ensembliste, maquette (Σ≅𝔓(𝒜)), discrete, point
ideas.modern_name: Spatial vs non-spatial locales/frames; atomic Boolean algebras; representation theorems for contact algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Locale theory (Ehresmann, Bénabou, Isbell, Johnstone 1960s–80s); Stone duality

ideas.what: Set-theoretic ateliers generated by ordered intervals as the basic tame example
ideas.modern_name: o-minimal structures (definable sets generated by intervals on an ordered line)
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984–86); van den Dries' book 1998
ideas.where_published: Esquisse §5 discusses tame/semianalytic structures in general terms

ideas.what: Infinite distributivity of the subobject lattice possibly implying faithfulness (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Frame law; spatiality / separation results for locales

missed.claim: Grothendieck's ateliers are, independently, a mereotopology: parthood ⊴, overlap/contact |∘|, well-inside ≪. They are aimed at tame topology and come with a classification of 'pointed' cases (Σ≅𝔓(ℒ)) and of maquettes. The literature on tame topology (o-minimality) and on region-based topology (contact/de Vries algebras, Whitehead-style point-free geometry) has not linked his 1986 programme to these frameworks.
missed.quote: atelier général (𝒜, ⊴, ≪, |∘|) … atelier ponctuel Σ ≃ 𝔓(ℒ) … maquette Σ ≃ 𝔓(𝒜)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This offers a point-free axiomatisation of o-minimal or tame geometry. One could compare it with de Vries duality and contact algebras, and with recent point-free and topos-theoretic treatments of o-minimality (e.g. spectral spaces of types, 'tame' locales).

missed.claim: The status and position of 'tame' (modéré) ateliers in the hierarchy, and whether tameness forces faithfulness, are left open.
missed.quote: NB Si les ateliers mod sont fidèles, le diagramme se simplifie, et mod se place entre at fidèl et maquette
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise, still unaddressed axiomatisation question: which point-free axioms characterise tame (o-minimal-like) region structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The atelier framework is a little-known unpublished axiomatic attempt at tame topology. This page is mainly a taxonomy, but it shows Grothendieck independently building a mereotopology with well-inside and contact relations, a link to region-based topology not recorded in the literature. No finished theorem is on the page.
transcription_corrections: Below 'Atelier général' the first coordinate is written and then overstruck; 'Atelier divisible' appears beneath, possibly crossed out.
In the paragraph: 'Je m'intéresserai plus particulièrement donc aux ateliers spatiaux*' (the line reads 'par les', then the paragraph runs on with 'des [-ens. ordo-] maquettes').

Last lines: 'qui incluent les maquettes) — Je présume qu'il y a lieu de supposer pour [les ateliers modérés qui sont aussi spatiaux, mais pas nécessairement locaux] et peut-être' continues overleaf with 'aussi que l'ensemble Σ … soit modulaire'.
The isomorphism signs in 'Σ≃𝔓(ℒ)' and 'maquette Σ≃𝔓(𝒜)' carry an overstrike; the reading is uncertain (possibly first written as ≠/≄ and corrected).
